fields.name: blue_deposited
fields.description: Initialize to zero if incoming memory is empty. Otherwise start from the incoming integer. Scan the supplied execution frames for a blue cube held before release, fingers opening at the bin-release pose, and subsequent empty-gripper withdrawal. This is positive evidence of a completed deposit. Override it only if the supplied interval unambiguously tracks that same carried cube through release to outside the bin. A same-color detection appearing after release, even near the release pose or withdrawing hand, does not by itself identify the carried cube. Do not infer identity continuity from color, proximity, or appearance timing alone. A detection appearing lifted off the table during release likewise does not by itself establish a failed deposit. An independently visible free cube, whether persistent or newly appearing and even of the same color, is not such evidence. The elevated release pose may project above and to either side of the bin center; that image-coordinate offset alone does not establish an outside release. The interval may begin at the release pose: neither a visible approach nor direct visibility of entry into the opaque bin is required. Use continuity within the interval to distinguish the carried cube from other free cubes; their persistence or appearance does not invalidate the deposit, and total visible cube count need not decrease. Increment once per such completed deposit in this interval. Use the held cube's color before release; do not count pickup, issuing B, repeated post-release frames, or unrelated cubes appearing or disappearing. Elevated wrist coordinates need not equal the bin's visible center. Preserve if no blue deposit is observed. e.g. 1

field blue_deposited, ANNOTATOR PROMPT

Policies consequently continued picking cubes instead of stopping, or wrote an increment that disagreed with the annotation. This breaks PREDICTABILITY and, at later decisions, SUFFICIENCY. Remove the episode-specific enumeration and the claim that all other supplied episodes remain zero. This field universally holds the cumulative integer number of successful blue deposits completed by the current decision step. Initialize to 0; increment once at the first decision step following each completed blue release into the bin; preserve at pickup and otherwise. Count the final deposit too. For example, after the third blue deposit in the three-blue/two-green task, write 3.

field red_deposited, ANNOTATOR PROMPT

Policies either wrote the correct increment contrary to the annotation or later lacked the prior red count needed to stop. This breaks PREDICTABILITY and SUFFICIENCY. Remove the episode-specific enumeration and the claim that all other supplied episodes remain zero. This field universally holds the cumulative integer number of successful red deposits completed by the current decision step. Initialize to 0; increment once at the first decision step following each completed red release into the bin, including the final deposit; preserve at pickup and otherwise. For example, after completing both red deposits in the two-red/one-green task, write 2 and retain it throughout the subsequent green pickup and deposit.

For mixed goals, the blanket green-first rule also selected the wrong color for the two-red/one-green goal, while no color priority covered the three-blue/two-green goal. These are SUFFICIENCY failures in target and color selection, separate from the erroneous zero-count annotations. Keep updating counters before choosing actions; retain C when all quotas are met, B when a requested cube is held and quotas remain, and A with an empty hand and an unmet quota. Replace blanket mixed red/green green-first priority with goal-conditioned priorities: complete green before blue for three blue and two green; complete green before red for two red and three green; complete red before green for two red and one green. Retain the existing green-first preference for the previously covered mixed layout with the bin near [130, 117]. For one red with the bin near [112, 177], choose red near [79, 127]. For two blue with the bin near [122, 181], choose blue near [91, 163] and [97, 117] at blue_deposited=0 and 1 respectively. For two red and one green with the bin near [107, 86], choose red near [74, 98] and [64, 83] at red_deposited=0 and 1 respectively; once red_deposited=2, choose green near [105, 117]. refused
  Reports repeatedly suggested that the policy prompt for memory might need an exception explaining why a visible release did not count, including a possible exception at the final deposit. The complete trajectories show successful deposits, not evidence for failed releases. The existing policy prompt already recognizes the carried cube's color, release, disappearance, and empty-gripper withdrawal, without requiring wrist coordinates to coincide with the bin center. It also already excludes unrelated free-cube appearances and disappearances. Keep that policy prompt unchanged and correct the annotations instead; no terminal exception is warranted. Likewise, do not adopt target-selection conditions predicated on zero counters after successful deposits. Those reported zeros were annotation errors: second and third pickups must use cumulative counts of one and two. Missing prior-deposit history is resolved by filling the existing counters correctly, not by adding new memory fields.

field blue_deposited, POLICY PROMPT
  During the three-blue task, a held blue cube ceased to be held as the fingers opened at the bin-release pose, and the empty gripper withdrew while other free blue cubes remained visible. The policy preserved 1 rather than writing the annotated count 2 and then selected the wrong next cube. Requiring visible disappearance inside the opaque bin made the update ambiguous, breaking PREDICTABILITY. Keep this field as the cumulative integer number of completed blue deposits, initialized to 0. Increment once when the supplied interval shows a blue cube held before release, opening fingers at the bin-release pose, and subsequent empty-gripper withdrawal. Direct visibility of entry into the opaque bin, a reduction in the total number of visible cubes, and equality between elevated wrist coordinates and the bin's image center are not required. The interval may begin at the release pose; an approach need not be visible. Distinguish the carried cube from other free cubes using the supplied interval rather than treating newly appearing or persistent cubes as evidence that release failed. Preserve otherwise; do not count pickups, issuing B, or repeated frames of one release. Example value after two completed blue deposits: 2.

field red_deposited, POLICY PROMPT
  During one-red and mixed red-and-green tasks, a held red cube disappeared from the gripper as the fingers opened at an elevated bin-release pose, followed by empty-gripper withdrawal. Other red cubes remained visible, including a separate cube already present before release. The policy preserved 0 instead of the annotated 1, sometimes continuing with A instead of stopping with C. This breaks PREDICTABILITY because the wording suggested that direct entry into the bin had to be seen. Keep this field as the cumulative integer number of completed red deposits, initialized to 0. Increment once when the current interval shows a red cube held before release, opening fingers at the bin-release pose, and subsequent empty-gripper withdrawal. Direct visibility of entry into the opaque bin, a decrease in visible cube count, and equality between elevated wrist coordinates and the bin's image center are not required. An interval beginning at the release pose is sufficient without a visible approach. Use within-interval continuity to distinguish other free cubes from the carried cube; their persistence or reappearance does not undo the deposit. Preserve otherwise, without counting pickups, issuing B, or repeated release frames. Example value after one completed red deposit: 1.

fields.name: blue_deposited
fields.description: Initialize to zero if incoming memory is empty. Otherwise start from the incoming integer. Scan the supplied execution frames for a blue cube held before release, fingers opening at the bin-release pose, and subsequent empty-gripper withdrawal. This is positive evidence of a completed deposit. Override it only if the supplied interval unambiguously tracks that same carried cube through release to outside the bin. A same-color detection appearing after release, even near the release pose or withdrawing hand, does not by itself identify the carried cube. Do not infer identity continuity from color, proximity, or appearance timing alone. A detection appearing lifted off the table during release likewise does not by itself establish a failed deposit. An independently visible free cube, whether persistent or newly appearing and even of the same color, is not such evidence. The elevated release pose may project above and to either side of the bin center; that image-coordinate offset alone does not establish an outside release. The interval may begin at the release pose: neither a visible approach nor direct visibility of entry into the opaque bin is required. Use continuity within the interval to distinguish the carried cube from other free cubes; their persistence or appearance does not invalidate the deposit, and total visible cube count need not decrease. Increment once per such completed deposit in this interval. Use the held cube's color before release; do not count pickup, issuing B, repeated post-release frames, or unrelated cubes appearing or disappearing. Elevated wrist coordinates need not equal the bin's visible center. Preserve if no blue deposit is observed. e.g. 1

Preserve otherwise; newly appearing free cubes do not cancel completed deposits. e.g. 1
